_comment: SF Symbols rendered on macOS 27.2.1 (26B131) by NSImage symbol images -> CoreUI vector glyph layers -> CGContext(PDF) -> pdftocairo -svg. Units are points at pointSize; SVG viewBox = NSImage.size (the symbol image canvas AppKit uses, including the symbol's built-in margins). Rects are [x, y, w, h] in SVG coordinates (y down). baselineY = text baseline inside the viewBox; capHeight = cap height of the matching SF Pro size; glyphRect = where AppKit places the glyph bitmap (2x pixel-snapped). Files: <symbol>.<weight>.svg = monochrome (black template); .hierarchical = layers with opacity 1 / 0.5 / 0.3 (primary/secondary/tertiary); .multicolor = system colours resolved in light (aqua) appearance; .var-N = variable value N/100 (inactive layers at opacity 0.3).

airdrop.note: Control Center AirDrop button. Private symbol (NSImage(systemSymbolName:) returns nil; rendered via +[NSImage imageWithPrivateSystemSymbolName:accessibilityDescription:]). ControlCenter binary references "airdrop"; CoreTypes com.apple.airdrop UTTypeSymbolName = airdrop. | finder: Finder sidebar AirDrop: CoreTypes com.apple.airdrop UTTypeSymbolName = airdrop (private symbol). | R3b-2: Apple screenshot (CC AirDrop tile).

appstore.note: Private symbol: the App Store "A" made of three strokes. Same glyph macOS uses for the Applications folder (CoreTypes com.apple.applications-folder UTTypeSymbolName = appstore), i.e. the Apps/Launchpad header glyph the PC drew.

backward.note: Now Playing previous-track button (filled, as the PC drawing). | R3b-2: Swift literals in ControlCenter + Apple screenshot.

forward.note: Now Playing next-track button (filled). | R3b-2: Swift literals in ControlCenter + Apple screenshot.

play.note: Now Playing play button (filled). | R3b-2: Swift literals in ControlCenter + Apple screenshot.

pause.note: Now Playing pause button (filled). | R3b-2: Swift literals in ControlCenter + Apple screenshot.

extras.why: empty outline to draw your own level into

battery.note: Menu bar battery. ControlCenter binary references battery.100percent / battery.25percent. The menu bar draws the charge level; battery.0percent is the empty outline if you fill the level yourself; battery.100percent.bolt is the charging glyph (multicolor = green fill, guess that the menu bar uses it). | R3b-2: the menu bar battery is not an SF Symbol: BatteryUIKit draws a 26x14 pt image (filled body + cap); see menubar[element=Battery] and menubar-battery-*.svg / png/menubar-battery-*.png.

bluetooth.note: Private symbol. ControlCenter binary references "bluetooth"; System Settings uses it too (CoreTypes com.apple.graphic-icon.bluetooth ISSymbolName = bluetooth). | settings: System Settings sidebar tile symbol for panes: bluetooth. Read from the pane extension Info.plist ISGraphicIconConfiguration or the CoreTypes graphic-icon UTI; the tile draws it monochrome white.

chevron.down.note: | finder: Toolbar group-by popup / list disclosure; Finder binary references chevron.down.

chevron.right.note: Submenu arrow (shell) and Finder Forward button. chevron.forward is the layout-direction-aware name; its SVG output is byte-identical to chevron.right in left-to-right layout. Finder binary references chevron.forward. | finder: Toolbar Forward. Finder binary references chevron.forward (byte-identical to chevron.right in LTR).

clipboard.note: Spotlight Clipboard mode (Cmd-4). Not verified against the live Spotlight UI.

display.note: Control Center Display module / Mission Control action. ControlCenter binary references "display".

doc.note: Spotlight Files mode and file rows. "doc" is a legacy alias of "document" in CoreGlyphs name_aliases.strings; both render byte-identical. Name kept as "doc" because CoreTypes (Finder sidebar Documents) references "doc". | finder: Sidebar Documents: CoreTypes com.apple.documents-folder UTTypeSymbolName = doc (alias of "document", byte-identical).

ellipsis.note: Apps (Launchpad) header more button; plain three dots as the PC drawing. | finder: Toolbar Action menu. Finder binary references ellipsis, ellipsis.circle and ellipsis.circle.fill; the PC drawing (from 27.2 screenshots) is plain dots. ellipsis.circle also rendered.

folder.note: Spotlight folder rows / New Finder Window action; filled like the PC drawing. Spotlight itself shows real file icons for folders. folder (outline) also rendered.

Read from the pane extension Info.plist ISGraphicIconConfiguration or the CoreTypes graphic-icon UTI; the tile draws it monochrome white.

keyboard.note: Outline keyboard; no current use in shell/.

lock.note: Lock Screen action; filled body like the PC drawing.

magnifyingglass.note: Menu bar Spotlight item and search fields. | finder: Toolbar search.

power.note: Restart / Shut Down / Log Out actions.

screen.mirror.note: Control Center Screen Mirroring. macOS uses two overlapping rectangles (ControlCenter binary references rectangle.on.rectangle and rectangle.on.rectangle.slash), not the old AirPlay screen-with-triangle the PC drew. | R3b-2: confirmed by the Apple 27 Control Center screenshot.

extras.why: menu bar Sound item, variable value

speaker.note: Control Center Sound slider glyph. ControlCenter binary references speaker.wave.2.fill, speaker.wave.3.fill and speaker.slash.fill. speaker.wave.3.fill is the menu bar Sound item; its .var-0 / .var-20 / .var-50 files are variable values 0, 0.2, 0.5 (0, 1, 2 waves lit; unlit waves at 30 % opacity, as AppKit draws them); the plain file = all lit. Hierarchical files: waves at 50 %; whether a system surface uses hierarchical here is a guess. | R3b-2: Apple 27 screenshot: Sound slider shows speaker.fill on the left and speaker.wave.3.fill on the right (~16 pt); see controlcenter entries.

square.grid.note: Spotlight Apps mode / Show Apps action; filled squares like the PC drawing. For the Control Center Stage Manager button macOS uses rectangle.3.group (ControlCenter binary reference), rendered as an extra. | R3b-2: Control Center Stage Manager button is sidebar.squares.leading (visual match with the Apple screenshot), drawn hierarchical.

sun.note: Control Center Display brightness slider and the light/dark action. Same symbol as System Settings Displays (CoreTypes graphic-icon.display). | R3b-2: Apple 27 screenshot: Display slider shows sun.min.fill left and sun.max.fill right (~16 pt).

terminal.note: New Terminal Window action. apple.terminal is the Terminal-app glyph (Finder references it); "terminal" is a near-identical older glyph, also rendered.

trash.note: Empty Trash action. | finder: Sidebar Trash / Move to Trash; Finder binary references trash.

wifi.note: Menu bar / Control Center Wi-Fi. The menu bar shows signal strength with variable value: .var-0 (nothing lit), .var-20 (dot lit), .var-50 (dot + middle arc lit), plain file = all lit; unlit parts at 30 % opacity, measured from AppKit. All wifi layers are primary, so hierarchical = monochrome (not rendered). | settings: System Settings sidebar tile symbol for panes: wifi. Read from the pane extension Info.plist ISGraphicIconConfiguration or the CoreTypes graphic-icon UTI; the tile draws it monochrome white.

toolbarGlyph.evidence: Same fit on the toolbar of that capture: magnifyingglass, square.grid.2x2 and squares.below.rectangle fit 13 pt/.large/.medium best (4-8 %); list.bullet, rectangle.split.3x1 (selected) and the disabled chevrons/tag could not be fitted cleanly.

finder.note: 13 pt with scale .large is not the same as a bigger point size at scale .medium: use these files (or scale the 32 pt files by the glyphRect ratio).

mapping.default: RegularLight (1): always the coloured tile, also in Dark appearance
mapping.dark: RegularDark (2, "Always"): dark tile in both appearances; the Dark style's "Automatic" sub-option is RegularAutomatic (0) = default tile in light, dark tile in dark
mapping.clear: ClearAutomatic (3); ClearLight 4 / ClearDark 5 force one appearance
mapping.tinted: TintedAutomatic (6), tint colour Automatic (follows the accent colour); TintedLight 7 / TintedDark 8

settingsIconStyles.answer: Dark appearance + style Default = the coloured light-style tile (identical bytes to <id>@<px>-light.png).
settingsIconStyles.thisMac: AppleIconAppearanceTheme = RegularDark -> dark tile in both appearances (= <id>@<px>-dark.png)
